clue.text: Commonly without money family gets in the way

indicators.note: the family group gets in, that is enters, the abbreviation for a road

parts.note: St, short for street, is a way
kin are one's family

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a family always seems to obstruct things when they are broke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commonly' marks the definition as slang: SKINT is informal British for penniless. 'gets in' puts KIN inside ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Skint is colloquial British slang for having no cash at all, so 'commonly' flags the informal register of being broke.

clue.text: Comedy hits get credit

parts.note: slaps are hits
tick is informal British for credit, as in buying on tick

explanation.surface: A comedy show's hits earn praise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On tick' is British slang for buying on credit.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapstick is boisterous physical humour, a broad style of comic performance.

clue.text: What a number of children!

parts.note: reads as an exclamation at a big family, but a number is also an edition of a magazine, and a person's offspring share that word

explanation.definitionFit: An issue is one number of a periodical, and in law a person's issue means their offspring.

clue.text: With two betters it could win place money

definitions.text: With two betters it could win place money

parts.words: With two betters it could win place money
parts.note: betters reads as gamblers, but means two horses better than it; a horse finishing behind two others may still pay out on a place bet

explanation.definitionFit: A horse finishing third, beaten by two superior runners, still earns a place payout in most each-way bets.

clue.text: For motorists what's pump-room for — to cure disorder?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: putting into disorder signals that the words to cure are scrambled

explanation.surface: A spa's pump-room, where people take the waters for a cure, imagined in a confused question.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pump-room' suggests a spa where one goes for a cure; for motorists it is the petrol-pump area in front of a garage. 'disorder' rearranges TO CURE into ECOURT after FOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A filling station's forecourt is where the petrol pumps stand, the motorist's own kind of pump room.

clue.text: It's quite a distance to drive, of course

definitions.meaning: on a golf course, the mown strip where one drives the ball

explanation.definitionFit: A fair way is a long way, and on a golf course the fairway is the closely mown stretch golfers aim their drives at.

clue.text: Soldier as local visitor?

definitions.meaning: a member of the ..., standing army
local is British for a neighbourhood pub; a frequent visitor there is its habitual customer

explanation.definitionFit: A regular is a professional serviceman, and also a pub's habitual customer, 'local' being British slang for one's neighbourhood pub.

clue.text: Caught girl the Indian shot

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
Anna is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl is caught and an Indian fires a gun.
explanation.walkthrough: Indian shot is the common name of a tropical plant, not a gunshot.
explanation.definitionFit: Indian shot is the popular name for the canna lily, from its hard round seeds like pellets.

clue.text: Wordsworth's Lucy got her living in these ways

definitions.text: Wordsworth's Lucy got her living in these ways

parts.words: Wordsworth's Lucy got her living in these ways
parts.note: got her living suggests earning, but alludes to Wordsworth's poem saying Lucy dwelt among paths few walked on

explanation.definitionFit: Wordsworth's poem opens 'She dwelt among the untrodden ways', describing paths no feet have walked.

clue.text: What's the date of touchdown, good man?

parts.note: a try in rugby is scored by touching the ball down
ST, saint, is a good man

explanation.surface: Asking a fine fellow which day the touchdown came.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby a TRY is scored by grounding the ball over the line, a touchdown.
explanation.definitionFit: A tryst is an arranged romantic meeting, a date between lovers.

clue.text: Very musical, Heather is overwhelming

parts.note: assai is the Italian musical direction meaning very
ling is a common name for heather

explanation.surface: Someone extremely tuneful named Heather is too much to bear.
explanation.walkthrough: Heather looks like a woman's name; it is the plant, LING.
explanation.definitionFit: Assailing means attacking hard, which an overwhelming force does to its victim.

clue.text: The Colonel sounds so mad

definitions.meaning: colonel is pronounced like kernel, and something like a kernel is nut-flavoured

explanation.definitionFit: A colonel sounds like a kernel, which is nutlike in character; and 'nutty' is slang for crazy or eccentric.

clue.text: Fastness John mapped

definitions.meaning: the quality of being fast, swiftness
John ... was a famous English mapmaker of the early 1600s

explanation.definitionFit: Fastness can mean rapidity of movement, and John Speed was the Stuart cartographer whose county maps are still reproduced.

clue.text: Circuitous royal progress?

parts.note: a royal progress is a formal tour; one that wanders around meeting the crowd is the informal stroll monarchs take among the public

explanation.definitionFit: A royal informal stroll among the public, wandering about to greet people, became the name for the Queen's crowd-greeting tours.

clue.text: Aim wildly at mysterious grey figures

indicators.note: aiming wildly means the letters of aim are thrown about
a mysterious, puzzling version of the word grey is one with its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: An archer shoots erratically at strange grey shapes in the gloom.
explanation.walkthrough: Two separate anagrams: 'wildly' turns AIM into IMA and 'mysterious' turns GREY into GERY.
explanation.definitionFit: Figures of speech, metaphors and similes, are what literary imagery consists of.

clue.text: Denies the East began conflict

indicators.note: in conflict, the letters of the two words fight and end up scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone denies that the East started the war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conflict' rearranges EAST BEGAN; 'the' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To abnegate is to renounce or refuse, giving something up or disclaiming it.

clue.text: Persuaded to join or back quiet oriental racket

indicators.note: going back means the word or is read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written
p, piano, is the musical mark for quiet
E for East, so eastern or oriental
din is a loud noise, a racket

explanation.surface: Someone is talked into joining a quiet Eastern racket, or else backing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns OR into RO; then P, E and DIN follow. 'racket' looks like crime but is noise.
explanation.definitionFit: To be roped in is to be talked or coaxed into taking part in something.

clue.text: Wine's nothing to Kenneth Ward in the City

parts.note: port is a fortified wine; with the 's it gives PORTS
O, zero, is nothing
Ken is short for Kenneth

explanation.surface: A wine means nothing to a man called Kenneth Ward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kenneth Ward' reads as a full name; Ward belongs to the definition. Portsoken is one of the wards (electoral districts) of the City of London.
explanation.definitionFit: The City of London is divided into wards, and Portsoken is one of them, on its eastern edge.

clue.text: Snare was effective as broadcast from various stations

parts.note: a net is a snare
worked means was effective

explanation.surface: A trap did its job, as broadcast on several channels.
explanation.walkthrough: A programme networked goes out from many linked stations at once.
explanation.definitionFit: A networked programme is transmitted simultaneously over a chain of linked stations.

clue.text: Cattle twitch, showing such energy

parts.note: kine is an old plural for cows, cattle
a tic is a nervous twitch

explanation.surface: Cows twitching show some liveliness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'such energy' refers back to the twitching: kinetic energy is the energy of movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Kinetic energy is the energy a body has because it is moving, as a twitching beast is.

clue.text: Farmer found frequently in royal company

indicators.note: in places the word for frequently within the royal pair

parts.note: two royals together: CR, Carolus Rex for King Charles, and ER, Elizabeth Regina
oft is an old word for often, frequently

explanation.surface: A farmer is often seen among the royal party.
explanation.walkthrough: CR and ER are royal cyphers, of a king Charles and Queen Elizabeth; put together they are royal company. A crofter farms a smallholding in the Scottish Highlands.
explanation.definitionFit: A crofter is a tenant smallholder in Scotland who works a small farm, a croft.

clue.text: Early device of cipher-breaking officer once?

indicators.note: the zero is breaking into the officer's title, splitting it

parts.note: a cornet was formerly the lowest commissioned officer in a cavalry troop
a cipher is a nought, the figure zero, O

explanation.surface: Wartime codebreakers' early gadget, used by some officer of long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Early' is read as Earl-y: a coronet is the heraldic device showing an earl's rank. 'Cipher-breaking' suggests codebreakers; it means O breaking into CORNET.
explanation.definitionFit: Peers' coronets in heraldry show rank, and the earl's coronet is the emblem that belongs to an earl.

clue.text: Range of borders for cloth

definitions.meaning: the ... Hills, a range along the English-Scottish border
a woollen fabric made from the wool of the sheep breed of that name

explanation.definitionFit: The Cheviots are hills on the Anglo-Scottish Border, and cheviot is a tweed woven from the wool of sheep bred there.

clue.text: Dance figures nothing to me

parts.note: eights are figures, numbers
O, the zero, is nothing

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs that dance steps mean nothing to them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'figures' looks like dance figures; here it is numerals, EIGHTS. An eightsome reel is a Scottish dance for eight people.
explanation.definitionFit: An eightsome reel is a Scottish country dance performed by eight dancers.

clue.text: Fix me up with night's lodging

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word me is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: a bed is a place to sleep for the night

explanation.surface: A traveller asks to be given a place to stay for the night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses ME to EM in this down clue; 'Fix me up' looks like a phrasal verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To embed something is to set it firmly into surrounding material, to fix it in place.

clue.text: East End hire organization belonging to third persons

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, here of East
an organization of the letters of hire is a rearranged order

explanation.surface: A hire company in London's East End is run by outsiders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East End' looks like London's East End but gives T, the last letter of East; 'organization' rearranges HIRE to HEIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Their is the possessive form of the third person plural pronoun, meaning of or belonging to them.

clue.text: Start work with a punch-up?

explanation.definitionFit: To set to is to begin a task energetically, and a set-to is a brief fight or argument.

clue.text: Dog with sound record

definitions.meaning: a separate recording, one song on an album

explanation.definitionFit: To dog someone is to tail or trail them, and a recorded song or band on an album is also called by this word.

clue.text: Dip articles after boiling initially

indicators.note: after says the articles come behind the opening letter
initially means taking only the first letter of the word boiling

parts.note: A and THE are the indefinite and definite articles

explanation.surface: Instructions to dip items into water once it has come to the boil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' gives two words, A and THE; 'after' puts them behind B from 'boiling initially'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dip is a quick swim, which is what going for a bathe means.

clue.text: Intelligence body, following tenuous Kremlin lead, tracked vehicle

parts.note: thin means slight or tenuous

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its opening letter, here of Kremlin

parts.note: a tank runs on caterpillar tracks

explanation.surface: A spy agency acts on a weak tip from Moscow and follows an armoured vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intelligence' and 'Kremlin' suggest spying, but the definition is a body of experts.
explanation.definitionFit: A think tank is a group of experts assembled to research policy, a body of brains.

clue.text: Would Eighth Army trooper run away twice?

parts.note: to desert is to run away from duty
to rat is to run away, abandon one's side

explanation.surface: A question whether a WWII soldier would twice flee his post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' says 'run away' is used for two words. Desert Rats was the nickname of British troops in the Eighth Army's North African campaign.
explanation.definitionFit: The Desert Rats were the 7th Armoured Division, fighting with the Eighth Army in North Africa.

clue.text: Saffron bloomers for such ladies

parts.note: bloomers suggests underwear, but the flowering autumn crocus, a saffron relative, is nicknamed after ladies without clothes because it flowers leafless

explanation.definitionFit: Autumn crocuses bloom without leaves, so country people call them naked ladies, bare of any covering.
